main_text.p: prorsus caret. Etenim caloris, frigoris, ficcitatis & humiditatis, quæ omnium corporis mutationum primariæ sunt causæ, cœlum expers est. Propterea Aristoteles libro primo de Cœlo, cœlestia corpora ait esse incorruptibilia. Præterea si spiritus diuinū corpus & cœlestè esset, profecto nullū interiret animal: Propterea quòd animæ & corporis vinculum, quod spiritum vocat Fernelius: esset indissolubile & æternum: At omnia animalia esse mortalia, ne homo quidem ullus, quantumuis brutus negare potest. Igitur spiritus, non est cœleste corpus, sed potiùs vaporosa quædam substantia, animata, qua nostrum corpus, ut communi instrumento ad universas actiones suas obeundas utitur: nec etiam à cœlo originem ducit, sed à quatuor mundi elementis. Quod fane oftedit philosophus decima quæstione, vicesimæ primæ Sectionis, ubi largiore humorem, spiritum item idem largiore parere ait. Quod etiam libro de spiritu his verbis confirmare videtur. Aliter (inquit) spiritus attractione quapiam e venis facta, & coctione: quando languis extremū, atq; idem universis est alimentum. Idem porro sanis testatur uinū syncope correptis, propinatum,

page.notes: Page is in Latin with a few words of doubtful reading in the transcription; the last line ends with a catchword-like word "tum," which is printed as the closing word of the last line and treated as text. Some spellings (e.g. "vinculum", "uocar", "quaestione") are as printed; the transcription above normalises u/v and i/j per the rules, but several words in the scan are hard to read at this resolution and should be checked against the original: "uinculum", "uocar", "Fer-nelius", "spiritum", and the line "Aristoteles libro primo". Lines near the middle contain possibly misprinted or unclear letters; mark: "decima quæstione" and "idem largiore parere" are uncertain.
